current_harness_support: The trusted fixture-host source now accepts the ten exact reviewed --cohort names as stable original rule-ID subsets. The runner passes each explicit ruleId for both selection and evidence state; legacy original/all and authored-cohort predicates remain unchanged. This descriptor grants no execution or project-policy authority, and no new named subgroup has executed in this worktree.
partition_policy: Select only the listed exact stable rule IDs through explicit trusted fixture-host cohort names, never row offsets, inferred severity filters or mutable source annotations. Source row order below is informational only.
Preserve every original positive/corrected-negative byte and original flags. This proposal neither changes authored_cohort metadata nor suppresses historical failures.
All 98 ordinary pairs, 16 unsupported graph plans and 443 mappings must remain visible in every future run; unselected or failed IDs are gaps, never hidden exclusions.
Each subcohort requires a fresh UUID, frozen source tuple, owner-approved bounded invocation and new exact nonserializable execution permit for each child-capable call.
Do not resume, merge receipts, pool execution budgets or attribute one run to another tuple. Separately executed subcohorts remain separate runs, not one qualified corpus.

The first three thematic parent names remain organizational only because their all-rerun plans exceed 48. The ten explicit smaller selector names implement the bounded partition; original_experimental is both its singleton theme and accepted singleton selector.
schedule_assumptions: Static transcription of current runFixtures/cohort scheduling: compatible stable flags group together; all phases except negative split declared severity and mapped backend.

Five phases can issue at most one conditional single rerun per selected ID: positive, negative, configuration, version and regression. Warnings can add one conditional suppression rerun; error suppression is mandatory and already counted.
Warning-disabled phase groups are counted separately; no per-ID disabled rerun is scheduled. Four actual control calls and one pre-runtime wrong-version denial are counted for each independent run.

Source-planned provider admissions are not compiler launches, receipts, pass claims or completion guarantees. Runtime failures, time/evidence limits or cleanup/quiescence failures can still leave a run partial.

empty_range_failure_retention.policy: Keep the deprecated -Xuse-fir-experimental-checkers flag and all global/raw warnings; no clean negative/configuration result is claimed or repaired by this partition. Historical failed receipts stay immutable and do not attest this new tuple.
